capitals.name: Belém (Belém do Pará)
capitals.note: The rebels held the provincial capital from 7 January 1835; they lost it between the July events and their 14 August 1835 attack (the page gives no day), held it again from 14 August 1835 to April 1836. Coordinates from the gazetteer.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, Cliopatria has no row. The page names Belém as the only place the rebels held; the 60 km radius is the researcher's reading of the city and its surroundings. The rebels lost Belém between the July events and 14 August 1835 and retook it that day (ledger; the page gives no day for the loss). The shape ends with the April 1836 loss of Belém: the page says the rebels then 'continued to resist from the interior of the province' but names no interior place and no gain of ground, so no rebel shape is drawn for 1836-1840 (repair 2026-10-19, following the reviewer: the interior is left to empire-of-brazil's contest of Pará, 1835-1840). No area on the page (the infobox gives 'Grão-Pará' as location and about 25,000 insurgents), so no area comparison.

region.text: the city of Belém: 'On the night of January 6, 1835, the rebels attacked and conquered the city of Belém'

ledger.note: 6 January 1835: the Cabanos take Belém. 'On the night of January 6, 1835, the rebels attacked and conquered the city of Belém'; 'On January 7, Malcher was released and was chosen as president of the province'.

region.text: Belém, lost to the imperial forces between the July events and the rebels' 14 August attack; the page gives no day

ledger.note: July-August 1835 (the page's sequence; no day given): the rebels lose Belém. Francisco Vinagre 'was not able to keep his supporters faithful' and would have yielded the government to imperial control 'in the person of marshall Manuel Jorge Rodrigues in July 1835', but 'the intervention of his brother Antônio' stopped it: the handover did not happen. The page then has the rebels, weakened by imperial forces and a returning squadron, lose the city: 'the rebel forces were destroyed and retired toward the interior', before 'they again attacked Belém on August 14'. Month 7 follows the page's order (the July events come first); the page dates neither the loss nor the retreat. The Portuguese page (https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabanagem) tells the handover differently (Vinagre agreed it in exchange for an amnesty and Rodrigues did not honour it) and gives no date for the loss either.

region.text: Belém, retaken after nine days of fighting

ledger.note: 14 August 1835: the rebels retake Belém. 'they again attacked Belém on August 14' and 'retook the capital'; Eduardo Angelim then presides.

region.text: Belém, abandoned under blockade and bombardment

ledger.note: April 1836: the rebels abandon Belém. The government attacked 'the capital again' in April 1836 and the rebels 'decided to abandon the capital'; Grenfell's ships 'blockaded and bombarded Belém'; the page has Angelim flee 'on May 10'. From then the rebels 'continued to resist from the interior of the province'.

region.text: the interior of Pará where the last rebels held out; the page names no place, so the province minus the Belém ring stands for it

ledger.note: 1840: the last Cabano group yields. 'In 1840 the last rebel group, under the leadership of Gonçalo Jorge de Magalhães, yielded'; 'amnesty was declared to the rebels in 1839'; infobox 'Result: Empire of Brazil victory', more than 40,000 dead. The region is the empire-of-brazil dossier's zone for the contest (the province of Pará) less the Belém ring, since neither the English page nor the Portuguese page (it says only that the cabanos in the forest 'lutaram até 1840') names an interior stronghold.

wars.name: Cabanagem

wars.outcome: Imperial victory: Belém lost by the rebels between the July events and 14 August 1835 (no day on the page), retaken on 14 August 1835, abandoned in April 1836 under naval blockade; resistance from the interior to the 1839 amnesty and the 1840 surrender; 'more than 40,000 dead'.
wars.note: The page gives the rebellion's population cost as 100,000 falling to 60,000 over five years, and also '30-40% of the population died'; the two figures disagree.

certainty.note: The rebels held a city and then an unnamed interior; no boundary is described on the page.

Reopened 2026-10-19 for the repair.

sources.title: Cabanagem (Portuguese Wikipedia)
sources.note: Opened for the repair: names no interior stronghold (no Santarém, Cametá, Vigia or Rio Negro); 'Os cabanos que se encontravam na selva lutaram até 1840'; Angelim taken in October 1836; the Vinagre-Rodrigues handover told as an agreed deal for amnesty; gives no date for the July-August 1835 loss. Cited in the notes of ledger/1 and ledger/4, not as an event source.

notes:
Cliopatria has no row. Counterpart string used by the empire-of-brazil dossier: 'Cabanagem rebels' (contest 1835-01 to 1840, whole province of Pará); this slug is its dossier. Type rebel (rule 5): hatched in its own colour while it holds ground.
Repair 2026-10-19 (reviewer verdict fail): (1) the 1835-07 loss of Belém no longer claims a handover to Rodrigues; the English page says it would have happened 'but for' Antônio Vinagre's intervention, the rebels lost the city later by force of arms, and the page gives no day: month 7 is the page's order, confidence 2. (2) The 60-300 km ring of 1836-1840 is removed; the rebel shape ends with the April 1836 loss of Belém, and the interior is left to empire-of-brazil's contest (a rebel presence there is drawn by that blend, not by a shape). The dissolve of 1840 and the war zone use Pará minus the Belém ring, as the empire-of-brazil dossier draws the province.
Thin: the English and the Portuguese pages (both opened) name no interior stronghold (Santarém, Cametá, Vigia, Rio Negro are not on either); a gap-filler needs a source beyond Wikipedia (the Portuguese page says only that the cabanos in the forest fought until 1840 and were 'completamente exterminados'). Disagreement between pages: pt tells the Vinagre-Rodrigues deal as made (an amnesty for the rebels, Rodrigues did not honour it); en says Vinagre would have yielded but for his brother. The dossier follows en and leaves the pt reading in the note of ledger/1. The pt page also dates Angelim's capture to October 1836 in a jungle hut; en has him flee on 10 May 1836 (ledger/3).
